name: Omar
overview: Omar was a male Edomite, known as the son of Eliphaz and a chief within the Edomite community. His identity is firmly rooted in his lineage and tribal affiliation, marking him as a significant figure among the descendants of Esau. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Omar means "speaker," reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew context. This name is recorded in Genesis 36:11 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Omar is explicitly identified as the son of Eliphaz, establishing his place within the Edomite family line. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for Omar.
scriptureSignificance: Omar's significance lies in his role as a chief of Edom, indicating a position of leadership and authority among the Edomites. His mention in the genealogical records in Genesis highlights the organized structure of Edomite tribes and their leaders. As a descendant of Eliphaz, Omar contributes to the biblical understanding of Edomite heritage and governance.
